current_component_sources.quote: A more consequential opening has emerged in quantum memory. Building on an existing 3D passive-memory proposal, we have a candidate construction that replaces its higher-body interactions with local three-body qubit interactions while retaining long-lived thermal storage under a specified noise model. Two internal reviews have checked different parts of the argument and caught corrections that are being incorporated. If the full proof holds, this would make an abstract protected-memory design closer to the kinds of interactions hardware can implement. It is not yet a practical memory: the required temperature and interaction strengths may be extremely demanding, and efficient initialization and robustness to general hardware errors remain open. It has not had external review.

current_component_sources.quote: I’ve put the quantum-memory construction through a stricter resource check. The proof’s current sufficient temperature scale is extraordinarily small, and I cannot yet show how to load a qubit into the required thermal state efficiently. The very small bound is a conservative proof guarantee, not a demonstrated physical lower limit. So my assessment is: potentially meaningful mathematics about which interactions can retain a thermal memory, but not yet a credible practical memory breakthrough. The next attack is the actual write/loading operation and whether the resource bounds can be improved.
current_component_sources.range_scope: Complete candidate memory/resource update,approximately07:14 observation after07:05marker;partial reviews/corrections and loading obstruction retain source scope.

current_component_sources.quote: There’s a useful improvement to the quantum-memory route: a different three-body qubit construction has an internally checked energy-scale guarantee more than 100 million times larger than the first one. It uses more connections between the auxiliary qubits, so that gain has a hardware cost. The important caveat is that the actual memory temperature requirement is still much colder than that number alone suggests, and we still haven’t established efficient, fault-tolerant writing or robustness to general hardware noise. So I’m not yet calling it a practical memory.
current_component_sources.range_scope: Complete distinct-variant energy-scale comparison,extra auxiliary connections,temperature and fault-tolerant writing/general-noise limits;not a temperature factor.

current_component_sources.quote: The memory work has made progress on the noise question: we now have an internally checked extension for a specified class of microscopic interacting baths, rather than relying only on an idealized noise equation. It still assumes a particular correlated thermal starting state and an ideal write/read interface. That makes the storage argument stronger, but it does not solve the practical task of preparing that state or writing into it reliably. The result is also not a guarantee against arbitrary hardware noise. I’m focusing on those missing operations.
current_component_sources.range_scope: Complete checked microscopic-bath storage extension,particular correlated thermal start and ideal I/O assumptions;not arbitrary hardware-noise/preparation/writing theorem.

current_component_sources.quote: On the memory’s loading problem, we now have an internally checked ideal preparation method for the auxiliary part, including its thermal fluctuations. That removes one of the missing pieces I mentioned earlier. It does not yet prepare the complete memory state: the correct distribution of the memory’s error patterns still has to be generated, and noisy writing remains unresolved. The sufficient operating conditions for this version are also extremely demanding, so there is still no practical device claim.
current_component_sources.range_scope: Complete chronological source-reported internal ideal preparation check;auxiliary step then complete isolated state,not noisy writing or joint bath preparation.

current_component_sources.quote: A meaningful update on the memory: we now have an internally checked ideal preparation procedure for the complete isolated memory state, not just its auxiliaries. It combines a way to sample the required error patterns with the auxiliary preparation, and is designed to preserve a qubit entangled with another system. This closes a mathematical loading step I previously said was missing. It still assumes ideal active controls and extremely demanding fixed operating conditions. Reliable noisy writing, preparation together with the actual bath, and a practical advantage over active error correction remain unproved. The result has not been externally reviewed.
current_component_sources.range_scope: Complete chronological source-reported internal ideal preparation check;auxiliary step then complete isolated state,not noisy writing or joint bath preparation.

proof_availability.classification_scope: The initial CANDIDATE three-body local-qubit reduction of an unnamed3D passive-memory proposal retains its two partial internal reviews,corrections being incorporated and conditional full-proof status. A reported DIFFERENT three-body qubit variant has an internally checked ENERGY-SCALE guarantee MORE THAN100MILLION TIMES larger than the first,but uses MORE AUXILIARY-QUBIT CONNECTIONS. This is not a100million-fold temperature or lifetime improvement;actual temperatures remain much colder than the energy-scale figure suggests. The internally checked STORAGE EXTENSION covers a SPECIFIED CLASS OF MICROSCOPIC INTERACTING BATHS with a PARTICULAR CORRELATED THERMAL STARTING STATE and IDEAL WRITE/READ supplied. Later source updates first report INTERNALLY CHECKED IDEAL AUXILIARY PREPARATION INCLUDING THERMAL FLUCTUATIONS,then an INTERNALLY CHECKED IDEAL PROCEDURE FOR THE COMPLETE ISOLATED MEMORY STATE by combining required ERROR-PATTERN SAMPLING with auxiliary preparation. It is designed to PRESERVE A QUBIT ENTANGLED WITH ANOTHER SYSTEM. This closes the reported MATHEMATICAL ISOLATED LOADING STEP at its stated scope. IDEAL ACTIVE CONTROLS and EXTREMELY DEMANDING FIXED OPERATING CONDITIONS remain assumptions. RELIABLE NOISY WRITING,PREPARATION TOGETHER WITH THE ACTUAL BATH and PRACTICAL ADVANTAGE OVER ACTIVE ERROR CORRECTION remain UNPROVED;the result has NOT BEEN EXTERNALLY REVIEWED. No arbitrary hardware-noise guarantee follows.
